title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: The practical route to usable CPL brightness is to keep a chiral, somewhat low-symmetry Eu(III) site while maximizing absorption and sensitization, as in tetrahedral Eu4 cages and hfa/pybox complexes, rather than maximizing glum alone.
explanation: Eu4L4 cages with chiral BINAPO combine 5D0→7F1 |glum| of about 0.20 with quantum yields near 81% in CHCl3, and the cage chirality can be retained after substitution by achiral dpepo (chiral memory). [(Eu(hfa)3)(S)-Bn-pybox] reaches |glum| 0.26–0.36 and the highest cited BCPL for 5D0→7F2 (465 M^-1 cm^-1 in dichloromethane) because low microsymmetry boosts both the 5D0→7F2 branching ratio and magnetic-dipole character of the 5D0→7F1,2 manifold. Two-photon-excitable PyBox complexes and aggregation-induced emitters are presented as further ways to raise brightness.
scope: Solution Eu(III) polynuclear cages, heteroleptic hfa complexes, and related aggregates aimed at devices or imaging.
conditions: Cage spectra at 2.5×10^-6 mol L^-1 in CHCl3; Bn-pybox data in acetonitrile and dichloromethane.
caveats: Individual glum and quantum-yield numbers are compound-specific. A later alkyl-ammonium tetrakis(camphorate) reaches glum = −1.54 but is cited for naked-eye detection, not as the brightness optimum.
